newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET - Jayasuriya misses record, S. Lanka set one.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Jayasuriya misses record, S. Lanka set one.

text.p: Sanath Jayasuriya missed out on Brian Lara's world record score of 375 but Sri Lanka broke the record for the highest innings total in test cricket on the final day of the first test against India on Wednesday.
Th Sri Lankans had compiled 952 for six, beating England's 903 for seven against Australia at The Oval 59 years ago, when the match ended in a draw.
The longstanding record was broken during the final session of a match which saw just 14 wickets fall over five days.

While the Sri Lankan team celebrated their achievement, the day was a personal disappointment for gifted opener Jayasuriya - and for the 30,000 spectators admitted free on the final day only to see him miss out the world record.
Jayasuriya's attempt to break Trinidadian Lara's four-year-old record 375 ended in failure when he was dismissed after adding just 14 runs to his overnight 326.
He was caught by Saurav Ganguly off Rajesh Chauhan in the fourth over of the day.
Jayasuriya's marathon 578-ball innings lasted 799 minutes and included 36 fours and two sixes. It was the fourth highest innings in tests after Lara's 375, Garry Sobers' 365 and Len Hutton's 364.
Jayasuriya's dismissal followed that of his longstanding partner Roshan Mahanama for 225 in the previous over. The pair put on 576 -- a record for any wicket in test cricket.
It fell short by just two runs of bettering the all-time record of 577 for first-class matches set by V.S.Hazare and Gul Mohammed for Baroda against Holkar in 1946-47.
The left-handed Jayasuriya began the day confidently by hitting three fours. He added two further singles before a tired looking stroke gave Ganguly a catch at silly point.
His anguish over being dismissed was evident as he banged the ground with his bat before walking away from the wicket. A packed stadium rose to applaud him all the way back to the pavilion.
Mahanama fell leg before to leg spinner Anil Kumble. He batted for 753 minutes, faced 561 balls and hit 28 fours.
A disappointed India captain Sachin Tendulkar said he blamed the wicket and not his bowlers for Sri Lanka running up a world record total.
"It was a terrible toss to win on such a wicket. I give a lot of credit to my spinners as it was not easy to bowl 70 overs each on this wicket," Tendulkar said.

"But by blaming the wicket I am not taking the credit away from the two batsmen since it requires a lot of courage and concentration to bat for two days. There are not many people who have done it," Tendulkar said.
Sri Lanka captain Arjuna Ranatunga said more than Jayasuriya the team wanted him to break Lara's record. "The manager and the team were more worried about it than Jayasuriya himself."
"It was one of the best wickets I have played on as a batsman, not as a bowler," said Ranatunga, who also scored a quick-fire 86.
India batted for the first two days to declare their first innings at 537 for eight before Sri Lanka batsmen took over and began piling up runs.
The hapless Indian bowlers had no respite even after they had dismissed both Jayasuriya and Mahanama within two balls of each other at the same total 615 early on Wednesday.

Aravinda de Silva, with his 12th Test hundred (126), and fifties from skipper Arjuna Ranatunga (86) and 20-year-old test debutant Mahela Jayawardena (66) ensured that Sri Lanka broke the the 59-year-old record.
Pandemonium broke loose outside the stadium when the police was unable to control the large number of spectators who were allowed in free to witness Jayasuriya's attempt at the record.
The security personnel manning the stadium proved insufficient as spectators scaled the high iron gates surrounding it to catch a glimpse of the action.
The police was then forced to baton charge sections of the crowd.
